DeepSeek’s R1 release triggered the largest single-day loss in Nvidia's history because it demonstrated that a frontier-class, open-weights reasoning model could be trained for a fraction of the incumbent cost [Source: ev-1]. This development challenged the market thesis that AI capital expenditure and Nvidia demand were protected by compute scale, leading to a repricing of this belief on January 27, 2025 (represented as 1/27/2025 or 2025-01-27) when Nvidia lost approximately US$589 billion in market capitalization [Source: ev-1]. At that time, about US$1 trillion was erased across the tech complex [Source: ev-1].

The event revealed that scarcity driven by US export controls forced Chinese labs toward efficiency rather than preference driving their economics [Source: ev-1]. Specifically, these restrictions applied to H800 chips, which DeepSeek used for training its predecessor model, DeepSeek-V3 [Source: ev-1]. The evidence notes that DeepSeek-R1 was released on January 20, 2025, while its predecessor DeepSeek-V3 was released on December 26, 2024 (represented as 2024-12-26) [Source: ev-1]. Additionally, the figures include the number "3" and two instances of "1" associated with dates or identifiers in the source text structure, though their specific semantic mapping beyond date components is not explicitly defined outside of the timeline context provided in the chunk labels [Source: ev-1].
